newsitem.title: USA: Drillers lifted by Santa Fe, momentum investors.
newsitem.headline: Drillers lifted by Santa Fe, momentum investors.

text.p: Shares of offshore drilling companies were lifted by the sector's earnings momentum and the likelihood that a share offering for Santa Fe International will be oversubscribed, analysts said.
A source familiar with the Santa Fe deal said the offering was well oversubscribed and the 30 million shares would be offered at $24-$27 on Monday.
The offshore and land drilling company is being sold by Kuwait Petroleum Corp. Investors unable to sate their demand in that offering are putting money into other drillers.

"Santa Fe is a high-quality offering and will be a huge, liquid stock which investors expect will trade up on its first day, so they are putting in big orders," said Ravi Kamath, analyst at Jefferies & Co.
The sector as a whole is benefitting from a switch out of technical stocks, where earnings momentum is slowing.
At midday, Falcon Drilling Co Inc was up 1-7/8 at 49-7/8, Transocean Offshore Inc was up one at 73-1/8, Ensco International Inc was up 1-5/8 at 55-1/8, and Marine Drilling Cos was up 1/4 at 19-3/4.
Global Marine was unchanged at 23-3/4 and Noble Drilling Corp added 1/8 to 22-7/8.

Iain Smith, analyst at Rodman & Renshaw, said, "These companies have very good earnings visibility and the sector has further to go once investors realize that their profitability has decoupled from the oil price."
There is more value to be unlocked in stocks such as Reading & Bates Corp if it can divest its development company, analysts said. R&B was up 1/2 at 26-3/4.
"The sector is now hot after the downgrades and slide in prices in March and April," said Kamath at Jefferies.
Kamath's top pick in the sector is Pride Petroleum Services, which was unchanged at 22-1/8.
Smith likes Transocean for its ultra-deep water exposure.
